notes:
Approved as currently stated by the owner ruling of 2026-09-07, recorded in verification/reviews/rulings/thm-0076-dependency-closure-2026-09-07.md. This record is a mechanical transcription of that ruling against the digest of the registry entry as it stands; the justification was not altered to accommodate it. The measurement record is verification/reviews/packets/escape-hatch-site-registration-2026-09-07.md.

OPENS THE ASSUMPTION AXIS, for this subject only. Until this record and ASM-0046's, verification/reviews/assumption/ did not exist and no assumption in the registry carried a record on its own axis — the state thm-0094-python-sdk-root-2026-09-03.md recorded. That is not repaired here for the other 44; each is its own subject and its own reading.

NAMEABILITY, NOT MEANING, and the entry is right to say so. Verus cannot reason about a type it has no declaration for, and these types live in production modules the prover does not read under the verify feature. What is trusted is the CORRESPONDENCE — that each Ex… declaration lists the same variants and fields as the type it names — and it is trusted only for the parts Verus cannot check itself, notably that a transparent mirror does not silently omit a variant a proof then treats as unreachable. No impl, no derive, no accessor is in scope.

REGISTRATION IS PER SITE, and that is what makes this reviewable at all. The entry names 27 Ex… declarations in mcp-re-http-profile/src/verus_std_specs.rs individually, so an Ex… declaration added, removed, or changed in shape is an unregistered site rather than something a mechanism-name whitelist would have absorbed silently. The review requirement says exactly that, and the entry's digest participates in every in-scope unit's trusted_assumptions, so widening it takes those units dirty.

THE OPACITY DECISION IS NOT HERE. Three of these types must additionally be opaque, and hiding a representation and mirroring one are different decisions; that is ASM-0046, approved separately and on its own terms.

It stops being acceptable if a mirror is edited without the type it mirrors, or if a proof begins to depend on a field the mirror declares but the type no longer has.
